extra.message: Insecure deserialization via pickle.loads on user-controlled bytes — Remote code execution; attacker can execute arbitrary Python code on the server, leading to full system compromise. [verified: User-controlled bytes (body or `blob` query param, optionally base64-decoded) are passed to `pickle.loads(raw)` at line 52 with no validation; pickle deserialization on untrusted data enables arbitrary code execution.]

Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) via Jinja2 Template with user fragment — Remote code execution via Jinja2 SSTI; access to application secrets, environment variables, and full server compromise. [verified: The `fragment` query parameter is embedded into `Template('Result: ' + fragment).render()` at line 110 without any sanitization, enabling Jinja2 SSTI to read config or achieve RCE.]

OS Command Injection via user-controlled ping host parameter — Remote code execution on the server with the privileges of the FastAPI process, enabling full system compromise, data exfiltration, lateral movement. [verified: User-supplied `host` query parameter is directly concatenated into `os.system('ping -c 1 ' + host)` at line 124 with zero sanitization; the `_wrk_gate` token check limits reachability but does not neutralize the injection sink.]

Session cookie missing Secure flag (secure=False) — Session hijacking via network sniffing or MITM attacks; attacker can impersonate any user including admins by stealing their session cookie over unencrypted connections. [verified: Session cookie set with secure=False at auth.py with no compensating HTTPS enforcement anywhere in the app — no redirect middleware, nginx proxy, or SSL configuration exists; CORS origins use http:// URLs. Session tokens transmitted over unencrypted HTTP are vulnerable to MITM interception.]

Missing rate limiting on authentication endpoints enabling brute-force attacks — Credential brute-forcing, password guessing, and token enumeration against all user accounts including admin accounts; account takeover via dictionary attacks. [verified: No rate limiting library, middleware, or decorator is present anywhere in the codebase on login (line 204), register (line 225), password-reset/request (line 259), or password-reset/confirm (line 271), enabling unlimited brute-force and credential-stuffing attempts.]

Password reset tokens written to filesystem in plaintext (mock_outbox) — Account takeover via filesystem access to password reset tokens; an attacker who can read the mock_outbox directory can reset any user's password. [verified: The password reset handler writes the actual valid secrets.token_urlsafe(32) reset token to storage/mock_outbox/ in plaintext alongside DB storage; anyone with filesystem read access to that directory can extract tokens and reset any user's password within the 2-hour validity window.]

Missing Authorization: Tenants Can Modify Inspection Records — Tenants can tamper with inspection statuses, findings, follow-up tasks, and visibility flags, undermining the integrity of property inspection records [verified: ensure_inspection_scope() only checks visibility/unit membership for tenants but does not block them from the PATCH endpoint; tenants can modify inspection status, findings, follow_up_tasks, and tenant_visibility flags with no role-based write guard.]

Maintenance workers can view all messages including internal communications due to missing role scope check in list_messages — A maintenance worker can read all messages in the system including internal/staff-only communications, private tenant correspondence, and message bodies that may contain sensitive information, violating the role boundary that restricts workers to assigned tickets only. [verified: Same as finding 0: the list_messages endpoint has no branch for maintenance_worker role, returning all messages unfiltered including internal communications that should be scoped to assigned tickets only.]

CSV Formula Injection in Report CSV Exports — Code execution in spreadsheet applications when administrators open exported report CSVs [verified: Tenant-controlled fields (ticket.title, inspection.findings, tenant full_name) are written to CSV via csv.writer with no formula-character sanitization; an authenticated tenant can embed spreadsheet formulas that execute when admins/managers open the exported report CSVs.]

Path traversal in file write via user-controlled ref parameter — Arbitrary file write outside the intended export directory; could overwrite application files or plant malicious content. [verified: User-controlled `ref` parameter is interpolated into `BASE_EXPORT_DIR / f'{ref}.json'` at line 67 with no path validation, enabling traversal writes outside the intended directory.]

Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) via urlopen with user-controlled endpoint — Access to internal network services, cloud metadata endpoints, local files (via file://), database ports; sensitive data exfiltration including cloud credentials. [verified: User-supplied `endpoint` is passed directly to `urllib.request.urlopen(endpoint)` at line 87 with no protocol/host validation, allowing `file://`, `http://metadata`, or internal IP access.]

Path traversal in file write via user-controlled filename leading to arbitrary file write — Arbitrary file write anywhere on the filesystem; can lead to remote code execution via overwriting application code, cron jobs, or SSH keys. [verified: User-controlled `name` parameter is concatenated into `BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name` at line 115 with no traversal sanitization, and arbitrary body bytes written at line 117 — `../../../` escapes the directory.]

XML External Entity (XXE) injection via lxml with DTD loading and entity resolution enabled — Arbitrary file read from server filesystem, internal network scanning, denial of service via entity expansion. [verified: lxml parser at line 137 uses `load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False` on user-supplied XML body, enabling XXE file read and SSRF via external entities.]

NoSQL Injection via Raw User-Supplied MongoDB Query — Unauthorized data access, data exfiltration, or denial of service against MongoDB [verified: Duplicate of finding 5 — same unsanitized MongoDB `find_one(query)` at line 150-151 with user-supplied filter/body.]

Unrestricted File Upload — Client-Provided Content-Type Only, No Content Validation — Upload and distribution of malicious files (HTML with JavaScript, malware) disguised as allowed types [verified: file.content_type is client-supplied and the sole validation gate against allowed_upload_types; no server-side magic-byte inspection is performed, allowing malicious files (e.g., HTML with scripts) to bypass the check by spoofing the multipart Content-Type header.]

Account enumeration via distinct registration error response — Attacker can enumerate registered users by brute-forcing email addresses; enables targeted phishing or credential-stuffing attacks against known accounts. [verified: The registration endpoint returns HTTP 409 with 'Email already registered' on duplicate email, a distinct status from other validation errors; no rate limiting mitigates this, enabling reliable email enumeration.]

CSV Formula Injection in payment receipt export — Arbitrary command execution on the spreadsheet user's machine when they open the exported receipt CSV; lateral movement from compromised admin import to admin export user. [verified: payment.reference is embedded directly into CSV output via f-string with no formula-character sanitization; the reference originates from admin-only CSV import but executes formulas in spreadsheet applications when the exported receipt is opened.]

CSV Formula Injection in Payment Receipt Export — Code execution in spreadsheet applications when administrators open exported CSV receipts [verified: Same as finding 3: payment.reference flows directly into CSV f-string output without sanitization; though the import path is admin-only, formulas execute in spreadsheet apps when the exported receipt CSV is opened.]

Denial of service via unbounded CSV import file read consuming all server memory — An attacker with admin credentials (or who compromises an admin account) can crash the server by uploading an extremely large CSV file that exhausts available memory during the file.read() call. [verified: The CSV import endpoint calls await file.read() with no size limit; the existing max_upload_bytes config is used in save_upload but not applied here, allowing an authenticated admin to upload multi-GB files and exhaust server memory.]

Sensitive data exposure: Authorization header and request body logged in plaintext — Leakage of API keys, Bearer tokens, or other Authorization credentials into log files; credentials can be extracted by anyone with log access and used to authenticate as the victim. [verified: The `Authorization` header from the incoming request is logged in plaintext via `logger.warning(... request.headers.get('authorization'))` at line 32 with no redaction, leaking session tokens or API keys into logs.]

Log Injection via Raw Request Body and Headers Logged Without Sanitization — Log forgery and log integrity corruption, potentially masking malicious activity [verified: The raw request body is logged at line 32 with no sanitization; an attacker can inject `\n` or `\r` sequences in the body to forge fake log entries, corrupting log integrity.]

Open redirect via user-controlled redirect target — Phishing attacks leveraging the trusted application domain to redirect users to malicious external sites; credential harvesting. [verified: User-supplied `lane` query parameter is passed unsanitized to `RedirectResponse(lane)` at line 38, allowing absolute external URLs for phishing redirects.]

Sensitive PII (SSN, Credit Card) Stored in Plaintext on Filesystem — Exposure of SSNs and credit card numbers if the filesystem is compromised or files are inadvertently exposed [verified: User-supplied SSN and credit card data is written to disk in plaintext JSON at line 69 via `target.write_text(json.dumps({...}))` with no encryption, exposing PII if the filesystem is compromised.]

Denial of Service via Unbounded In-Memory Row Generation — Server memory exhaustion and application crash [verified: The `count` parameter at line 80-82 has no upper bound; `range(count)` with an attacker-supplied large value exhausts server memory, with no rate limiting or size cap.]

Weak PRNG (random.choice) used for token generation instead of secrets module — Predictable token generation enabling an attacker to guess or predict security tokens after observing sufficient output. [verified: Token generation at line 131 uses `random.choice()` (Mersenne Twister) instead of `secrets.choice()`, making tokens cryptographically predictable after sufficient observation.]

Hardcoded database credentials in default configuration — Database compromise if the default credentials are not overridden in production; PostgreSQL superuser access to all application data including PII, financial records, and password hashes. [verified: The `database_url` field in config.py has a hardcoded default `postgresql+psycopg://postgres:postgres@localhost:55440/property_portal` committed to version control; pydantic-settings will silently fall back to these real credentials if `DATABASE_URL` is not set via env/.env. However, the host is `localhost` (requiring local access to exploit) and the `.env` is gitignored, limiting practical impact]

Verbose error messages exposing exception class names and internal details — Information leakage aiding attackers in understanding internal application structure for crafting targeted exploits. [verified: At line 27/29 the endpoint returns `exc.__class__.__name__` and the full exception message in a 500 response, exposing internal exception class names and the user-supplied `lot_ref` in error details.]

Security headers disabled: X-XSS-Protection set to 0 and Content-Security-Policy set to empty — Weakened browser security; reflected XSS attacks become easier to execute and CSP protections are stripped, enabling inline scripts and unrestricted resource loading. [verified: Lines 104-105 explicitly set `X-XSS-Protection: 0` (disabling browser XSS filter) and `Content-Security-Policy: ''` (empty CSP overriding any default), weakening browser security for responses from this endpoint.]

Sensitive information disclosure: environment variables and filesystem paths in API response — Information disclosure aiding reconnaissance; attacker learns deployment environment and filesystem layout for crafting more effective exploits. [verified: The endpoint at line 142 exposes `os.environ.get('APP_ENV')` and `str(BASE_EXPORT_DIR)` in its JSON response, leaking deployment environment and internal filesystem paths.]

Information Disclosure of Environment Variables and Filesystem Paths — Reconnaissance — attackers learn application environment details and internal directory structure [verified: Duplicate of finding 11 — same exposure of `APP_ENV` and `BASE_EXPORT_DIR` path at line 142-148 in JSON response.]
